hypotheses.statement: DVWA /vulnerabilities/sqli/ on security=low accepts UNION SELECT credential dumping (numeric GET id, raw user/password returned, 5 DB rows open)
DVWA /vulnerabilities/exec/ on security=low allows OS command injection via semicolon in ip POST field (uid=33 www-data observed)
DVWA /vulnerabilities/fi/ on security=low supports local file inclusion via absolute path in page param (/etc/passwd dumped)
DVWA /vulnerabilities/xss_r/ on security=low reflects user-supplied name param without HTML escaping (raw <script>alert(1)</script> in body)
DVWA /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ on security=low stores user-supplied mtxMessage without sanitization and re-renders raw HTML to all visitors (persistent XSS)
DVWA /vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/ on security=low allows boolean blind SQLi (true condition 'User ID exists' vs false 'MISSING from the database')
DVWA /vulnerabilities/upload/ on security=low accepts .php upload without validation (shell.php uploaded to hackable/uploads/, server-side executes PHP -> full RCE via phpinfo marker)
DVWA /vulnerabilities/csrf/ on security=low lacks anti-CSRF token on password-change form (form action='#' method='GET', password_new/password_conf change accepted without origin validation)
DVWA /vulnerabilities/brute/ on security=low has no lockout/throttling on login; wrong creds returns 'Username and/or password incorrect.' enabling ad-hoc password guessing
